goal: Split the oversized host and compiler translation units along their existing seams and lock the result with a line-ceiling ratchet, without changing any observable language or runtime behaviour
new_in_2_9_9: src/mellowlang/host/runtime.py is a 66-line assembler over host/base.py plus fourteen host/families/<name>.py registration modules; the 204-syscall registry, its order, its costs, and every handler result are unchanged
argument-shape predicates shared by more than one syscall family live in host/families/support.py

native/standalone/src/mellowc.c keeps scanning, parsing, and statement dispatch while the while-loop shape recognizers and their fused emitters moved to mellowc_fastloops.inc, included by that one translation unit so CMake needs no change
tests/language/test_source_structure.py carries LINE_CEILINGS: a file over 1,000 lines must be declared and no declared file may exceed its ceiling, so the budgets only move down
the workspace boundary gate treats native/standalone .inc fragments as C surface, so they cannot reach the Python layer either
docs/PROJECT_STRUCTURE.md documents the module boundaries and the project skill records the split seams plus the rule that the native job needs an explicit cmake --build before CTest
runtime_notes: no syscall, opcode, bytecode layout, or CLI output changed in this patch
the encrypted save envelope (ChaCha20Poly1305 with HKDF) stays a Python service until phase 2
MELV standalone CLI hooks remain Python-side and are scheduled after the storage migration
green threads stay cooperative and explicit-yield based
the standalone heap registry is still a linear scan with no automatic GC trigger, which is the measured cost behind money/ledger throughput on the native surface
runtime_policy: Native C is the release-authoritative runtime for v2.9.9 core work
default C execution must fail fast when native support is missing
release and CI validation should include native-only execution plus sanitizer/fuzzer gates
a file split must be verbatim and proven by before/after equivalence, not by review
